title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is not a manuscript page of the 1976 divided-power de Rham notes. It is a typed page, p. 57 of Exposé IX, 'Modèles de Néron et monodromie', from SGA 7 I (Grothendieck, published in LNM 288, 1972). It is evidently interleaved in cote 136: the neighbouring pages are handwritten computations with divided-power differential algebras S{U_0..U_m}[dU_0..dU_m].

Setting: A_K is an abelian variety over the fraction field K of a henselian DVR with base S, and A'_K is its dual. T_ℓ denotes the Tate module, viewed for ℓ = p as a pro-system of finite flat group schemes (a Barsotti–Tate pro-group). Superscript f is the 'fixed' part, coming from the connected Néron model, and superscript t is the toric part.

§5.2.6 finishes the proof of the orthogonality theorem 5.2 under semi-stable reduction. The claim is (T_ℓ(A'_K)^f)^⊥ = T_ℓ(A_K)^t, which by orthogonality is equivalent to T^t ⊂ T^f.
- For ℓ ≠ p this follows from the Galois criterion 3.5.
- For ℓ = p (indeed for any ℓ), the argument is a rank count. The left side is canonically the Cartier dual D(T'/T'^f). Its height is 2n − 2α − μ, which equals μ because semi-stability gives λ = 0 and so n = α + μ. That is also the height of T^t.
- The inclusion T^t ⊂ T is 'strict', meaning a monomorphism at every finite level. Hence T^t is maximal among Barsotti–Tate sub-pro-groups of T of the same height, and equality follows.

§5.3 begins: orthogonality between strict BT sub-pro-groups of the dual pro-groups T_ℓ(A_K) and T_ℓ(A'_K) yields, from (5.2.2), an induced pairing T_ℓ(A_K)^ab × T_ℓ(A'_K)^ab → T_ℓ(G_m). Here T^ab = T^f/T^t, the Tate module of the abelian part of the reduction. This is the pairing later refined in the monodromy-pairing sections of Exposé IX.
errors: No mathematical error. The rank computation 2n−2α−μ = μ is correct given λ = 0 (n = α+μ).

Mild gap as presented on this page: concluding equality from maximality needs an a priori inclusion T^t ⊂ (T'^f)^⊥, i.e. that T^t lies in a BT subgroup of the same height. That inclusion is presumably supplied by (5.2.2) or earlier parts of §5, not on this page.
Typos in the original typescript: 'du systèmes projectifs'; 'il s'ensuit' (fine) and 'équiv aut' (typing gap).

ideas.what: Orthogonality theorem: under semi-stable reduction the toric part of T_ℓ(A) is the exact orthogonal of the fixed part of T_ℓ(A'), including ℓ = p via Barsotti–Tate pro-groups
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck's orthogonality theorem for Néron models / semi-stable reduction

ideas.what: Height/maximality argument for strict sub-Barsotti–Tate pro-groups
ideas.modern_name: Equality of p-divisible subgroups of equal height with an inclusion

ideas.what: Induced pairing on abelian parts T^ab × T'^ab → T(G_m)
ideas.modern_name: Weil pairing on the abelian part of the reduction (precursor to the monodromy pairing)

missed.claim: Archival note: a typed page of SGA 7 Exposé IX (p. 57) is interleaved in cote 136, among the 1976 handwritten divided-power de Rham notes. It is likely scrap paper reused or misfiled; the handwritten computations may be on its reverse. There is no mathematical connection between the two sets of material.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a verbatim typed page of the published SGA 7 Exposé IX. It contains nothing unpublished and nothing uncredited.
transcription_corrections: The transcription is essentially faithful to the typescript.
